title: Completeness of compact continuous-function spaces
statement:
Let $S$ be a compact Hausdorff topological space and $V$ a complete normed additive commutative group. The continuous functions $C(S,V)$ form a complete normed additive commutative group with pointwise operations and supremum norm
$$\|f\|=\sup_{s\in S}\|f(s)\|,$$
where the norm of the unique function on the empty space is zero. The norm topology is the compact-open topology. If $V$ is a normed vector space over a normed field $K$ (a field [def-weil-field] with a multiplicative absolute value and its associated metric), pointwise scalar multiplication makes $C(S,V)$ a normed $K$-vector space.
